intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September from London

selected_hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
selected_hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24h petrol station near the bus terminal or a kebab shop near Lagos center (~€3-5)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro–Lagos bus ticket online at rede-expressos.pt to save time. The hostel is a short walk or cheap taxi (~€5) from Lagos bus station. Keep energy for tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy the hostel's communal area. Walk to the historic old town of Lagos — explore the 16th-century city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the free Igreja de Santo António exterior and the nearby Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, ~€3 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, a long golden beach just east of Lagos (15-min walk or free bike from hostel if available). Swim, relax, and soak up the September sun. The crowds thin out in mid-September making it ideal. Explore the rock formations at Ponta da Piedade on foot (30-min walk from town) — stunning golden cliffs and sea caves, completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lagos marina at sunset. Enjoy the lively atmosphere of Rua 25 de Abril, Lagos's main bar street. Grab a cheap beer or glass of local Algarve wine at one of the outdoor terraces.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mulher de Capote near the hostel — coffee + pastel de nata for ~€2
meals.lunch: Grab a prego (steak sandwich) or bifana at a local tasca near the market for ~€4-5
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local tasca on Rua do Ferrador — prato do dia (dish of the day) with wine for ~€8-10

day_by_day.notes: September weather in Algarve is warm (24-28°C) with minimal rain — perfect beach weather. Bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (EVA Bus line, ~€2.50) or rent a bicycle (~€10/day from Lagos bike shops) to Praia da Luz, a beautiful village beach 6km west of Lagos. Arrive early to enjoy the calm morning sea and dramatic red cliffs. Walk the coastal path along the cliffs for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue west by bus or bike to Burgau, a tiny whitewashed fishing village with a quiet beach. Explore the village, chat with locals, and enjoy the authentic Algarvian atmosphere. Return to Lagos by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) area for a walk. Head to Rua 25 de Abril for the evening — many bars offer happy hour deals (2-for-1 cocktails, cheap wine). Try a glass of local Algarve wine such as Vida Nova or Quinta dos Vales.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen DIY or local padaria (bakery) — toast, coffee, juice for ~€2-3
meals.lunch: Fresh fish sandwich or grilled sardines at a beach snack bar in Praia da Luz for ~€6-8
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — grilled fish or cataplana for ~€10-12 with house wine

day_by_day.notes: Burgau is a hidden gem — far fewer tourists than Lagos. The coastal walk between Luz and Burgau is about 5km and takes ~1.5 hours if you choose to hike it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — take the EVA Bus from Lagos bus station (~€4.50 each way, ~1 hour). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a 15th-century fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe. Walk the clifftop paths with stunning Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or hitch to Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta in Sagres — wild, windswept beaches popular with surfers. Explore Cabo de São Vicente (Cape St. Vincent), the most southwestern point of continental Europe — free to visit, just €1 for the lighthouse museum. Watch the famous sunset here.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Relax at the hostel and socialize with fellow travelers. Join a hostel-organized pub crawl or social event if available.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at the hostel or a café near the bus station for ~€2
meals.lunch: A Tasca in Sagres village — grilled fish of the day with salad and bread for ~€9-11
meals.dinner: Back in Lagos — Nah Nah Bah burger bar or a cheap pizza place on Rua 25 de Abril for ~€8-10

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is windier and cooler than Lagos — bring a light jacket. The last bus back to Lagos is around 19:30-20:00, so check the EVA timetable in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak or join a budget group kayaking tour from Lagos marina (~€20-25 per person) to explore the famous sea caves and grottos at Ponta da Piedade. This is one of the most iconic experiences in the Algarve and well worth the splurge.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, relax at Praia do Camilo — a small, sheltered beach near Ponta da Piedade accessible via wooden stairs. Swim and sunbathe. Walk back to Lagos along the clifftop trail (free, ~45 minutes).
day_by_day.evening: Saturday night in Lagos is lively. Head to the marina area for sunset drinks, then explore the old town nightlife. Try a ginjinha (cherry liqueur) shot at a local bar for €1-2.

meals.breakfast: Café Golfinho near the marina — full Portuguese breakfast (eggs, toast, coffee) for ~€4-5
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — buy bread, cheese, local presunto (ham), and fruit from the Mercado Municipal for ~€5
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon or a local tasca — try arroz de marisco (seafood rice) shared between two for ~€12-14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayak tour in advance on weekends as they fill up quickly. Alternatively, rent a kayak independently for ~€15/hour from the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train from Lagos station to Portimão (~€2.50, 20 minutes). Walk to the famous Praia da Rocha — one of the Algarve's most spectacular beaches with towering orange cliffs. Arrive early on Sunday to get a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Portimão town center — visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays!) housed in a former sardine canning factory. Walk along the riverside promenade. Browse the Sunday market if running.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Sunday evenings are quieter — enjoy a peaceful dinner and early night. Walk along the Lagos waterfront at dusk.

meals.breakfast: On the train or grab something at Portimão station café for ~€2-3
meals.lunch: Praia da Rocha beachfront — grilled sardines and salad at a local restaurant for ~€8-10
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Lagos — traditional Portuguese home cooking, prato do dia for ~€7-9

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Rocha can be crowded on weekends but is stunning. The Museu de Portimão is excellent and free on Sundays — highly recommended for understanding local fishing history.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take the bus or a rideshare to Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (~30 min from Lagos). Book a budget wine tour and tasting in advance (~€15-20 per person). The estate produces award-winning Algarve wines and has beautiful sculpture gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, head to nearby Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry). Walk the old town and admire the Gothic cathedral (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus or train via Tunes. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the hostel. Share wine recommendations with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen or local padaria for ~€2-3
meals.lunch: Picnic with wine and local cheeses purchased at the winery shop or a café in Silves for ~€6-8
meals.dinner: Café Restaurante Rui in Silves (if still there) or back in Lagos — try local cataplana de frango for ~€9-11

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales is one of the most accessible wineries from Lagos. Alternatively, Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) near Guia is another option. Always book wine tours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve beaches by local bus. Head to Praia de Odeceixe — a stunning river-meets-sea beach on the border of Algarve and Alentejo (~1.5 hours by bus via Aljezur, ~€5-6). Arrive mid-morning and enjoy the unique landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at Odeceixe beach and explore the charming village of Odeceixe perched on the hill above. Walk the trail along the river estuary. This area is part of the Costa Vicentina Natural Park — wild and unspoiled.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus (check return times carefully — last bus can be early). Enjoy a quiet evening in the hostel common room.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel before catching the bus — bread, coffee, fruit for ~€2
meals.lunch: Restaurante Cego in Odeceixe village — fresh fish and local wine for ~€10-12
meals.dinner: Self-catering at the hostel kitchen — buy ingredients from the local Pingo Doce supermarket for ~€4-6

day_by_day.notes: Check EVA Bus schedules carefully for Odeceixe — service is limited. The last return bus is often around 17:00-18:00. This is one of the most beautiful and least-visited beaches in the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Lazy morning in Lagos. Visit the Farmers' Market at Mercado Municipal (open mornings, Mon-Sat) — buy fresh local produce, honey, almonds, and figs. Walk through the old town and visit the free Igreja de Santa Maria church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a free self-guided walking tour of Lagos using a downloaded map or free app. Visit the Forte da Ponta da Bandeira (€2 entry) — a 17th-century sea fort at the harbor entrance. Walk along the city walls and enjoy views over the bay.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening — visit a local wine bar in Lagos such as Adega Cantigas do Mar or a wine shop offering tastings. Try Algarve regional wines (Vida Nova, Quinta do Barranco Longo) for ~€2-4 per glass.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit, local bread, and cheese from the market for ~€3-4
meals.lunch: Snack bar near the beach — tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese) and coffee for ~€3-4
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) style dinner, share plates for ~€10-12 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Mercado Municipal is a great place to buy affordable local snacks and souvenirs. Algarve almonds, carob products, and medronho (arbutus berry spirit) make great budget gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Albufeira. Take the train from Lagos to Albufeira-Ferreiras station (~€5.50, ~1 hour), then a local bus to the beach strip. Visit Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in the old town — charming and less touristy than the strip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Albufeira's old town — whitewashed buildings, cliff-top views, and the famous tunnel to the beach. Visit Praia da Oura if you want a livelier beach scene. Walk the clifftop promenade for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a final evening stroll along the Lagos waterfront. Try medronho (local firewater) at a bar — usually €1-2 a shot.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at Lagos train station café for ~€2
meals.lunch: Restaurante A Ruína in Albufeira old town — grilled fish with sea views for ~€10-13
meals.dinner: Back in Lagos — O Trovador restaurant or similar for a traditional Portuguese dinner for ~€9-11

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira is more touristy and expensive than Lagos — stick to the old town for a more authentic experience. Avoid the strip restaurants which are overpriced.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Dona Ana — one of Lagos's most photogenic beaches, a 20-minute walk from the hostel. Arrive early to enjoy it before day-trippers arrive. Explore the rock arches and sea caves accessible at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Second winery visit — take a taxi or rideshare to Quinta do Barranco Longo near Carvoeiro (~30 min, share cost with hostel friends). Enjoy a tasting of their organic Algarve wines (~€10-15). Alternatively, visit Adega Cooperativa de Lagos for a more budget-friendly local cooperative wine tasting (~€5-8).
day_by_day.evening: Friday night in Lagos — lively atmosphere. Join the hostel social event or head to Rua 25 de Abril. Try a caipirinha or local wine at one of the outdoor bars. The area around Praça Gil Eanes is great for people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen or local café — yogurt, fruit, coffee for ~€2-3
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Dona Ana — fresh grilled fish or salad for ~€7-9
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina — splurge slightly on a seafood cataplana for ~€13-15 to celebrate the penultimate weekend

day_by_day.notes: Adega Cooperativa de Lagos on Rua do Ferreiro is a hidden gem for budget wine lovers — you can buy excellent local wine directly from the cooperative at very low prices (€3-5/bottle).

day_by_day.morning: Final beach day — head to Meia Praia for a long, relaxed morning. This wide sandy beach is perfect for a final swim. Rent a paddleboard (~€15/hour) or just relax with a book. Enjoy the warm September sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit the local shops on Rua 25 de Abril and Rua Cândido dos Reis for affordable souvenirs: local wine, almonds, carob chocolate, azulejo tiles, and cork products. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with hostel friends. Splurge slightly on a nice meal at one of Lagos's better restaurants. Walk the old town one last time at night — the illuminated city walls and cobblestone streets are magical.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at a café near the hostel — eggs, toast, ham, coffee for ~€4-5
meals.lunch: Picnic on Meia Praia — buy supplies from Pingo Doce supermarket for ~€5-6
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon or Casinha do Petisco — farewell dinner with local wine, budget ~€15-18 per person as a final treat

day_by_day.notes: Buy wine at the Adega Cooperativa de Lagos to take home — it's excellent quality and very affordable. Check airline liquid restrictions for carry-on. Pack wine in checked luggage with bubble wrap.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (store luggage if needed). Final morning walk through Lagos old town — grab a last pastel de nata and coffee at your favorite local café. Visit any spots you missed during the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, take the EVA Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Lagos bus station to Faro Airport (~€5-7, ~1.5 hours). Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in the Algarve!

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão (milky coffee) at a Lagos café for ~€2-3
meals.lunch: Light snack at Lagos bus station or Faro Airport — sandwich and juice for ~€5-7
meals.dinner: Airport or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Book the Lagos–Faro Airport bus in advance at rede-expressos.pt. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for the bus journey plus airport procedures. The bus stop in Lagos is at the main bus terminal on Rua Porta de Portugal.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked airport transfer or taxi (~1 hour) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack near the hostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or convenience store near the hostel – try a pastel de nata and a light sandwich

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – just arrival and settling in. Confirm all bookings for upcoming days. Lagos town center is walkable from the hostel. Rest well for a full Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lagos Old Town on foot – stroll through the historic center, visit the Igreja de Santo António (Church of St. Anthony) and the Municipal Museum. Walk along the city walls and enjoy the charming cobblestone streets waking up slowly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach (10-minute taxi or bus ride from Lagos center) – a long, golden sandy beach perfect for swimming, sunbathing, and getting your first taste of the Algarve coast. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella for a relaxed afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Wander the lively Rua 25 de Abril for bar-hopping and evening atmosphere. Enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar overlooking the marina.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel – espresso, fresh orange juice, and a croissant or tosta mista (~€5)
meals.lunch: O Camilo restaurant near Praia do Camilo – grilled fish of the day with salad and local bread (~€15–18)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos – traditional Portuguese cuisine, try the grilled sea bass or cataplana for two (~€20–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a local SIM card or confirm data roaming. Grab a Lagos town map from the hostel reception. September weather is warm and sunny – perfect beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia Dona Ana – one of Lagos's most iconic beaches, a short walk or 5-minute taxi from the hostel. Explore the dramatic golden cliffs, sea stacks, and crystal-clear turquoise water. Swim and snorkel in the calm morning waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal cliff path from Praia Dona Ana toward Praia do Camilo – a scenic 30-minute walk with breathtaking views of the Algarve coastline. Descend the wooden staircase to Praia do Camilo for more swimming and cliff exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Lagos, enjoy the sunset from Ponta da Piedade viewpoint (short taxi ride) – the most spectacular rock formation in the Algarve, glowing golden at dusk. Return to town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota near the hostel – fresh pastries, yogurt, and coffee (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Beach kiosk at Praia Dona Ana – grilled sardines, salad, and a cold Sagres beer (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco in Lagos – cozy tapas-style Portuguese restaurant, try the pica-pau (marinated pork) and local cheeses (~€18–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the cliff path. Bring sunscreen, water, and a hat. Ponta da Piedade is best visited 30–45 minutes before sunset for golden hour photography.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience – depart from Lagos by car or organized tour (~45 minutes east). Hike the dramatic limestone cliff trails above Praia da Marinha, one of the most photographed beaches in Portugal, with sea caves, arches, and hidden coves below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach for a swim in the stunning turquoise waters surrounded by towering cliffs. Explore the accessible sea caves and rock pools at low tide. Relax on the beach before heading back.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a quiet evening stroll along the marina waterfront. Browse the evening market stalls if available.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café before departure – toast, eggs, and coffee (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks brought from Lagos, or the small beach café at Praia da Marinha – sandwiches and cold drinks (~€10–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nah Nah Bah in Lagos – popular burger and craft beer spot for a relaxed Friday evening (~€15–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check tide times before visiting – low tide reveals the best sea caves and rock pools at Praia da Marinha. Wear water shoes for rocky terrain. Book the coastal hike experience in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Sagres – the southwestern tip of Portugal and Europe's 'end of the world.' Visit the impressive Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress) perched dramatically on the cliffs, with sweeping Atlantic Ocean views. Explore the historic wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Cabo de São Vicente – the most southwestern point of continental Europe. Walk the clifftops, visit the lighthouse, and watch the powerful Atlantic waves crash against the rocks. Browse the artisan market stalls near the cape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos (30-minute drive). Saturday evening in Lagos is lively – enjoy the buzzing atmosphere of the old town with street performers and busy terraces.

meals.breakfast: Café in Sagres town square upon arrival – fresh bread, local honey, and coffee (~€5)
meals.lunch: A Sagres restaurant near the fortress – grilled tuna steak (atum) with potatoes and salad, a local specialty (~€16–20)
meals.dinner: Taberna de Lagos – rustic Portuguese tavern with live fado music on weekends, petiscos (tapas) and wine (~€20–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rent a car or take the Eva bus from Lagos to Sagres (departures every 1–2 hours, ~€4 each way). Sagres can be windy even in September – bring a light jacket. Cabo de São Vicente is free to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Sunday morning in Lagos – sleep in, then visit the Lagos Farmers' Market (Mercado Municipal) for fresh local produce, cheeses, smoked meats, and artisan goods. A great opportunity to pick up local snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia da Luz – a beautiful, quieter beach 15 minutes west of Lagos by bus or taxi. Enjoy a peaceful Sunday afternoon swim in the calm bay, surrounded by red-ochre cliffs. The village of Luz has a charming seafront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beachfront bar in Praia da Luz, then return to Lagos for dinner. Sunday evenings are calm and perfect for a leisurely meal.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered from the farmers' market – local bread, cheese, fruit, and pastries enjoyed in a nearby square (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Luz beach – prego (steak sandwich), chips, and a cold drink (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: No Pátio restaurant in Lagos – Mediterranean-Portuguese fusion in a lovely courtyard setting, try the lamb or fresh fish (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos Farmers' Market is busiest Sunday mornings – arrive by 9:30 AM for the best selection. Praia da Luz is served by the Onda bus from Lagos (~€2 each way).

day_by_day.morning: Book the Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience – travel to the Lagoa wine region (~45 minutes east of Lagos). Join a guided winery tour to learn about the unique Algarve terroir, indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and the winemaking process.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a guided tasting of 4–6 Algarve wines paired with local cheeses, presunto (cured ham), and traditional cataplana (a slow-cooked seafood or meat dish in a copper pot). This is the heart of the experience – savor every bite and sip.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Visit a local wine shop to purchase a bottle of your favorite Algarve wine from the tasting. Relaxed evening in town.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or nearby café before departure – yogurt, fruit, and espresso (~€5)
meals.lunch: Included in the Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience – cataplana, bread, cheeses, and charcuterie with wine pairings
meals.dinner: Light dinner at Cervejaria Dois Irmãos in Lagos – fresh seafood, grilled prawns, and a glass of local white wine (~€18–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience at least 3–4 days in advance as spots fill quickly. Arrange transport to Lagoa – consider a taxi or joining an organized tour from Lagos. Designated driver or shared transport recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour – depart from Benagil Beach (~1 hour east of Lagos by car or organized tour). Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, with its cathedral-like domed ceiling and natural skylight. An unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, explore the Benagil and Carvalho beaches area. Praia de Carvalho is a hidden gem accessible via a short tunnel through the cliff – perfect for a post-kayak swim. Relax on the beach and enjoy the dramatic scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or transfer back to Lagos. Treat yourself to a well-deserved dinner after an active day on the water.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a café before departure – eggs, toast, and coffee (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Benagil Beach – grilled chicken piri-piri wrap and fresh juice (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant in Lagos – upscale-casual dining with excellent seafood risotto and Algarve wines (~€25–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour well in advance – it's one of the most popular experiences in the Algarve and sells out quickly, especially in September. Wear a swimsuit under clothes and bring a dry bag for valuables. Tours typically last 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves – the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (~40 minutes from Lagos by train or car). Book the Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk experience. Begin with a guided tour of the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves, with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Silves food walk through the charming old town – sample local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry brandy), almond sweets, local cheeses, smoked sausages, and traditional pastries at artisan shops and market stalls. Visit the Gothic Silves Cathedral.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train (scenic and affordable, ~€3.50 each way). Relaxed evening in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Café near Lagos train station before departure – pastel de nata and galão coffee (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Included in the Silves Food Walk – tastings of local products throughout the tour
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves (if staying later) OR back in Lagos at O Galileu – traditional Portuguese grilled fish and vegetables (~€18–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos–Silves train runs regularly (check CP Portugal timetable). The Silves Food Walk typically lasts 3–4 hours. September is harvest season in Silves – the orange groves and vineyards are beautiful. Buy a bottle of medronho as a souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia do Burgau – a picturesque, quieter fishing village beach 20 minutes west of Lagos. Explore the small village, watch local fishermen, and enjoy a morning swim in the sheltered bay. The beach is less crowded than Lagos beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Via Algarviana coastal section between Burgau and Salema (approximately 5 km, 1.5 hours) – a scenic clifftop trail with stunning Atlantic views, wildflowers, and birdwatching opportunities. Arrive at the charming fishing village of Salema for a swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by taxi or local bus from Salema. Enjoy a quiet evening with a sunset drink at a Lagos rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Café in Burgau village – fresh bread, local jam, and coffee (~€5)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Atlântico in Salema – fresh grilled fish overlooking the beach, a local institution (~€16–20)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Lagos – beloved local tasca (tavern) with daily specials, excellent value (~€15–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy walking shoes for the coastal hike. Bring water, sunscreen, and a light snack. The Burgau–Salema coastal path is well-marked but can be uneven in places. Check bus times from Salema back to Lagos in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Portimão – the Algarve's second-largest city, 20 minutes east of Lagos by train. Explore the revitalized waterfront and visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sunday, ~€3 other days) – an excellent museum in a converted sardine canning factory telling the story of the Algarve's fishing heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha – Portimão's famous beach, one of the Algarve's most spectacular, with golden sand, dramatic rock formations, and a lively promenade. Swim, sunbathe, and explore the rock formations at the western end of the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for the famous riverside sardine grills – September is still sardine season. The Portimão waterfront is lined with casual restaurants grilling sardines over charcoal. Return to Lagos by train in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Portimão near the train station – fresh pastries and coffee (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant at Praia da Rocha – grilled sea bream, salad, and local wine (~€18–22)
meals.dinner: Riverside sardine grill on the Portimão waterfront – grilled sardines, boiled potatoes, peppers, and a cold beer (~€12–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos to Portimão by train takes ~20 minutes and costs ~€2.50 each way. Praia da Rocha is a 15-minute walk or short taxi from Portimão station. The sardine grills on the waterfront are informal and excellent value – look for the smoke!

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak or SUP board from a Lagos beach rental shop and paddle along the Lagos coastline independently – explore the sea caves, arches, and hidden beaches around Ponta da Piedade at your own pace. A wonderful way to revisit the coastline from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return equipment and spend the afternoon at Meia Praia Beach for a final long, relaxed beach session. Swim, read, and soak up the September sun. This is your last full beach day – make the most of it.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos – splurge slightly on your last full evening. Explore the vibrant Saturday night atmosphere in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or café – full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, presunto, cheese, and coffee (~€7–9)
meals.lunch: Beach kiosk at Meia Praia – grilled chicken, salad, and a cold drink (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vasco da Gama in Lagos – elegant but mid-range, excellent cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana) as a farewell feast (~€28–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kayak and SUP rentals are available from several operators near Praia Dona Ana and the Lagos marina (~€15–25 per hour). Book the farewell dinner reservation in advance for Saturday evening. Pack and organize luggage tonight for the journey home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos – take a slow, nostalgic walk through the old town one last time. Visit your favorite café for a final espresso and pastel de nata. Browse any remaining souvenir shops for last-minute gifts – local almonds, carob products, Algarve wine, or handmade ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (standard checkout 11:00–12:00, confirm with hostel). Arrange transfer to Faro Airport (~1 hour) based on your departure flight time. Enjoy the scenic drive through the Algarve countryside one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, sea caves, coastal hikes, and Portuguese culture in the beautiful Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a Lagos café – espresso, fresh orange juice, pastel de nata, and a tosta mista (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café near the airport – soup, sandwich, or a snack (~€10–12)
meals.dinner: Airport or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before your flight for the transfer to Faro Airport plus check-in and security. Pre-book your airport transfer the day before. Store luggage at the hostel if you have time to spare before checkout. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer pre-arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (approx. 1 hour drive). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine prepared by the hotel. Light room service or a curated welcome amenity basket awaits.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.dinner: Light welcome snack/charcuterie board and Algarve wine provided by the hotel upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel. Pack light carry-on essentials for easy access after long travel day.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Take a gentle orientation stroll through Lagos old town — explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets to get your bearings after arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most elegant beach (10-minute taxi). Settle into a premium sun lounger with umbrella service, swim in the calm Atlantic waters, and enjoy the golden September sunshine. Alternatively, explore Praia do Camilo, a dramatic cove with stunning cliff formations just south of Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a top Lagos restaurant. Head to Casinha do Petisco or Restaurante Adega da Marina for refined Portuguese cuisine with fresh seafood. Enjoy grilled sea bass, percebes (barnacles), and a bottle of Alentejo white wine. After dinner, take a relaxed evening walk along the Lagos marina promenade.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh pastries, local cheeses, fruit, eggs, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light beach club lunch at Meia Praia Beach Club — grilled prawns, fresh salads, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco or Restaurante Adega da Marina — premium Portuguese seafood tasting menu with local wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: September weather in Algarve is excellent — warm and sunny with temperatures around 26–28°C. Perfect beach conditions. Book dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — depart by private transfer to Praia da Marinha (approx. 45 minutes east of Lagos). Embark on a guided coastal hike along one of the Algarve's most spectacular cliff-top trails. Marvel at dramatic limestone arches, hidden grottos, and turquoise coves. Descend to the beach for a refreshing swim in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Marinha coastline at leisure. Snorkel in the sea caves and rock pools. Enjoy a picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by your guide or head to a nearby beach restaurant. Return to Lagos by private transfer mid-afternoon and relax at the hotel's terrace with a glass of chilled rosé.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Lagos — try No Pátio or a hotel terrace with Atlantic views. Dinner at Restaurante Vitor's — one of Lagos's most celebrated fine dining establishments, known for creative Portuguese cuisine and an exceptional wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the tour guide or lunch at Restaurante Boneca Mar near Marinha beach — fresh grilled fish and local salads
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vitor's Lagos — tasting menu with wine pairing featuring Algarve and Alentejo selections

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer. The coastal path can be uneven. Book the guided hike experience in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — private transfer to Benagil Beach (approx. 50 minutes from Lagos). Join a premium small-group or private kayak tour to paddle through the world-famous Benagil Cave. Glide through sea arches, hidden beaches, and dramatic coastal formations. A truly bucket-list Algarve experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Benagil Beach or nearby Praia de Carvalho. Enjoy a leisurely lunch at a local restaurant. Return to Lagos by private transfer. Spend the late afternoon at leisure — perhaps a spa treatment at the hotel or a swim at Praia do Pinhão, a beautiful small cove near Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at A Forja restaurant in Lagos — a beloved local institution known for its authentic Portuguese dishes, generous portions, and warm atmosphere. Try the cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana) and pair with a crisp Algarve white wine.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — early start recommended for the kayak tour
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante O Litoral near Benagil — grilled octopus, fresh fish of the day, and local wine
meals.dinner: A Forja Lagos — traditional Portuguese cataplana and grilled fish with Algarve wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour well in advance — it is extremely popular. Opt for a private tour for a more exclusive experience. Bring waterproof bag for valuables. The cave is best visited in the morning when light streams through the ceiling opening.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience — private transfer to the Lagoa wine region (approx. 40 minutes from Lagos). Visit a prestigious local winery such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor for a guided vineyard tour. Learn about the unique Algarve terroir, grape varieties (Negra Mole, Castelão, Arinto), and winemaking traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a full tasting of premium Algarve wines — whites, rosés, reds, and a late-harvest dessert wine. Enjoy a traditional cataplana lunch paired with the wines, prepared by the winery's chef. Explore the estate grounds and olive groves. Return to Lagos by private transfer in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Lagos. Stroll through the historic Zona Velha (old town) and browse artisan shops. Aperitivo hour at a wine bar — try Adega Papagaio for an excellent selection of Portuguese wines by the glass. Light dinner at Taberna de Lagos — tapas-style Portuguese petiscos and natural wines.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Winery cataplana lunch with wine pairing at Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor — included in the experience
meals.dinner: Taberna de Lagos — petiscos (Portuguese tapas), local cheeses, charcuterie, and natural wine selection

day_by_day.notes: This is a highlight day for wine enthusiasts. Request a private winery tour for a more personalized experience. Designate a driver or use private transfer — do not drive after wine tasting. Purchase a few bottles to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of Europe. Private transfer to Sagres (approx. 35 minutes from Lagos). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched on towering cliffs. Walk the windswept headland and take in breathtaking Atlantic panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse — the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe. Feel the raw power of the Atlantic Ocean crashing against 75-meter cliffs. Visit the local artisan market near the lighthouse. Head to Sagres town for lunch. Spend the late afternoon at Praia do Martinhal, one of the most beautiful and sheltered beaches in the region.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at Restaurante Bossa in Sagres or return to Lagos for dinner at Restaurante Laranjeira — an elegant restaurant in a historic orange grove setting, known for its refined Portuguese cuisine and exceptional wine list.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — early start for Sagres
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Dromedário in Sagres — fresh tuna, grilled fish, and local Sagres-style dishes with ocean views
meals.dinner: Restaurante Laranjeira Lagos — refined Portuguese tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Bring a windproof jacket — Cabo de São Vicente is notoriously windy even in September. Sunset at the cape is spectacular and worth timing your visit around. Book dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk — private transfer to Silves (approx. 40 minutes from Lagos). Explore the magnificent Moorish red sandstone castle, one of the best-preserved in Portugal. Climb the battlements for panoramic views over the Algarve countryside, orange groves, and the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided food walk through Silves old town. Sample local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry spirit), almond sweets, local cheeses, smoked sausages, and traditional pastries. Visit the Silves Municipal Market. Explore the Gothic Cathedral of Silves. Return to Lagos by private transfer in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Enjoy a private in-room wine and cheese experience arranged by the hotel, or head to the hotel terrace for sundowners. Dinner at Restaurante O Camilo — perched dramatically above Praia do Camilo with stunning cliff views, serving exceptional fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Food walk tastings in Silves old town — multiple stops featuring local Algarve specialties (included in the experience)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camilo Lagos — fresh seafood with cliff-top views, premium wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Silves is particularly beautiful in September when the surrounding orange and almond groves are lush. The food walk is a wonderful cultural immersion. Book O Camilo dinner well in advance — it is very popular and has limited seating.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour — private transfer to Faro (approx. 1 hour from Lagos). Board a premium private boat for a guided cruise through the Ria Formosa lagoon system. Glide through tranquil channels, discover hidden barrier islands, spot flamingos, herons, and migratory birds, and learn about this extraordinary protected ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark on Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) — the most remote and pristine island in Ria Formosa. Swim in the crystal-clear lagoon waters, walk the untouched white sand beaches, and enjoy the serene isolation. Lunch at the island's acclaimed Estaminé restaurant — the only restaurant on the island, known for its exceptional fresh seafood. Return to Faro by boat and transfer back to Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos at Restaurante Casinha do Petisco — intimate, elegant setting with creative Portuguese cuisine. Try the black pork secretos, fresh local fish, and pair with a premium Alentejo red wine. After dinner, enjoy a nightcap at a Lagos cocktail bar.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — early start for Faro transfer
meals.lunch: Estaminé restaurant on Ilha Deserta — fresh oysters, grilled fish, and seafood rice with local wine (book in advance)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco Lagos — creative Portuguese tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat tour and Estaminé restaurant reservation well in advance — both are extremely popular. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and light layers for the boat. The Ria Formosa is a UNESCO-recognized biosphere and one of Portugal's Seven Natural Wonders.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury beach day at Praia de Dona Ana — one of Lagos's most iconic and beautiful beaches, just 2km from the hotel (short taxi or scenic walk). Arrange premium sun lounger and parasol service. Swim in the sheltered turquoise cove framed by golden limestone cliffs. Morning yoga session on the beach if available through the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the sea caves and rock formations at Ponta da Piedade — a short walk from Dona Ana beach. Hire a local fisherman's boat for a private 1-hour grotto tour of the spectacular Lagos coastline caves and arches. Return to the hotel for a luxurious spa afternoon — book a signature massage or treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Special evening: private sunset sailing cruise along the Lagos coastline. Sip champagne as the sun dips below the Atlantic horizon. Return to port and head to dinner at Restaurante Vitor's for a second visit or try Eleven Lagos — a sophisticated fine dining experience with panoramic views.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Praia de Dona Ana beach restaurant — fresh grilled fish, seafood salad, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Eleven Lagos or Restaurante Vitor's — premium tasting menu with wine pairing and Atlantic views

day_by_day.notes: Book the private sunset sailing cruise in advance through the hotel concierge. The Ponta da Piedade grotto boat tour is best in the afternoon when light illuminates the caves. September evenings are warm and perfect for outdoor dining.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Monchique — the lush mountain village in the Serra de Monchique (approx. 45 minutes from Lagos by private transfer). Explore the charming village, visit the Franciscan convent ruins, and hike to Fóia peak — the highest point in the Algarve at 902m — for sweeping panoramic views over the entire region and Atlantic coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monchique thermal spa town of Caldas de Monchique — a beautiful valley spa resort with natural mineral springs. Enjoy a thermal spa treatment or simply stroll through the elegant gardens. Sample medronho brandy at a local distillery. Return to Lagos by private transfer in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — a beloved waterfront restaurant with an extensive wine cellar and traditional Portuguese dishes. Try the grilled black pork, cataplana, and pair with a Monchique-region wine. Evening stroll along the Lagos marina.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Central in Monchique — traditional mountain cuisine featuring smoked meats, local cheeses, and Monchique honey with regional wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina Lagos — traditional Portuguese cuisine with premium wine selection and marina views

day_by_day.notes: Monchique offers a completely different landscape from the coast — lush eucalyptus and pine forests, cooler temperatures, and mountain air. Bring a light jacket. The contrast with the coastal Algarve is striking and refreshing.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine experience — visit a different Algarve winery for comparison. Head to Quinta da Penina or Herdade dos Grous near Albufeira (approx. 1 hour from Lagos) for a private vineyard tour and barrel tasting. Focus on premium red wines and reserve selections. Learn about the differences between Algarve's four wine sub-regions.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery visit, stop at Albufeira's old town for a brief exploration of the charming whitewashed streets and clifftop views. Visit Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in Albufeira old town. Return to Lagos by private transfer. Spend the late afternoon relaxing at the hotel or exploring Lagos's artisan boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner experience — book a private chef dinner arranged through the hotel, or dine at the most exclusive restaurant in the region. Try Restaurante Bon Bon in Carvoeiro (approx. 30 minutes) — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering an extraordinary tasting menu celebrating Algarve ingredients with world-class technique.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Winery estate lunch with wine pairing — included in the private tour experience
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon Carvoeiro (Michelin Star) — signature tasting menu with full wine pairing by the sommelier (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Restaurante Bon Bon requires advance reservation — book as early as possible, ideally before the trip. This is a bucket-list dining experience. Private transfer to and from Carvoeiro is essential for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final full morning — sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take a final walk through Lagos old town, visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), and browse the local artisan shops for last-minute gifts — local wines, almond products, hand-painted tiles, and cork goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final beach afternoon at Praia do Camilo — arguably Lagos's most beautiful small beach, accessible via a wooden staircase through the cliffs. Swim, sunbathe, and soak in the last of the Algarve sunshine. Alternatively, book a final spa treatment at the hotel for ultimate relaxation before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special Lagos restaurant — return to a favorite from the trip or try Restaurante Laranjeira for an elegant final evening. Toast to the journey with a bottle of premium Algarve wine. Pack and prepare for departure. Arrange private transfer to Faro Airport for the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the hotel — take your time and savor the last morning
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Lagos café — try Pastelaria Mulher de Capote for traditional pastéis de nata, local pastries, and coffee
meals.dinner: Restaurante Laranjeira Lagos — elegant farewell dinner with premium wine pairing and refined Portuguese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer for the following morning. Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed. Purchase any remaining wine or local products. Settle any outstanding hotel charges.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos — enjoy a last gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Check out and store luggage with the hotel concierge if the flight is in the afternoon. Take a final stroll to the Lagos waterfront and marina for a last look at the Atlantic. Collect any purchased wines or gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport (allow 1.5 hours for the journey plus check-in time). Depart the Algarve with extraordinary memories of beaches, wine, culture, and world-class cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — in-flight

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café near the hotel before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for the Faro Airport transfer — 1.5 hours minimum. Faro Airport can be busy in September (peak end of season). Ensure all purchased wines are properly packed in checked luggage with protective wine sleeves. Consider joining the TAP Air Portugal frequent flyer program for future Portugal trips.
